questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: English speaking destination was important to me, and then applied for big cities that had a reputable Uni and seemed like id be fun to go live in for a few months.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 10/10 would recommend!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Only thing I had to do when arriving was pick up my student card, which was communicated well by the host Uni via email, they also had a stand in the airport actually where I got brochures for the mandotory healthcare I had paid for before arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Didn't need any special assistance, so?

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Got it through AirBnb which was alright, and I found something also while there for 1000cad a month. You can also apply for co ops that are between 500-800.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Anywhere on or between bloor st and queen st should be perfectly fine, anywhere else I would research distance to campus and POIs. All of the greater toronto area is very safe, so that shouldn't be a concern.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No availablity for 1 sem exchange programs, and also quite expensive actually since you often have to get the meal plan if you want to live on campus

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite easy, they communicated well, most of it was self-service, didn't how to physically go anywhere are call someone.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Specific help for exchange students as a first line help-desk, generally quick respons times across departments. Pretty much any help imaginable is available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 4 for 4, so no complaint or compromises.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be deterred by being waitlisted on a course. It got all my courses and was waitlisted on 2 of them. Depending on the size of the course 50-200(from my experience with the 2 courses) drop off, leaving room for the people on the waitlist.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Similar to back home. Mostly very good programmes, but I had 1 course that wasn't as great while I was abroad.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Same level as back home

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I missed the well designed and prepared tutorials at UCPH where we practice what the teacher preach. It was a lot more self study here.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECO326
ECO380
ECO358
CSC108

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ECO380, highly recommend, it's an IO course, which I personally enjoy, combining known subjects for Micro II with more advanced game theory.
ECO326/ECO316 is pure game theory and goes hand in hand with ECO380
CSC108 was very satisfying for a non-programmer like me. It was fun to apply some theoretical math to practical problems.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great varsity games to go watch, and opportunities to join lower leagues through the Uni, as well as so many clubs (i.e. running club)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Quite a few. People handing out flyers all over campus for events, the excahnge office arranged events to, like a pub quiz and movie night. Also lots of athletic activities available. They have a swimming pool, tennis courts, multiple free gyms and drop in games for basket ball and football.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Football (NOT american football!)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Niagra falls, and go to british columbia or alberta for the lakes and mountains too.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, im like water ;)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in clubs do sports and show up for all of the exchange events. Especially exchange students are very eager to make friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tipping

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Definately not the tipping culture.
